tasks.title: SEO: complete and continuously verify the full technical checklist
tasks.acceptance: Audit every template for HTTP status, canonical URLs, robots/noindex, unique titles/descriptions, crawlable internal links, correct sitemaps/lastmod, rendered content, image alt/licensing, relevant schema, social previews, mobile performance and real translations/hreflang. Fix failures; archive dated URL-level evidence. Keep thin reference pages excluded.
tasks.next_action: Extend SEO-02 and existing publication checks into a template-by-template audit. Separate lab checks from field measurements; do not add unsupported ratings or schema.

tasks.title: Daily indexing: request 8-10 eligible URLs when Google quota permits
tasks.owner: MotorJury team + Adir for Search Console access
tasks.acceptance: Daily queue contains 8-10 new or materially improved reviewed, canonical, 200-response, indexable URLs when enough qualify and the actual console quota permits. tasks.title: Editorial: write interesting original articles in natural human language
tasks.acceptance: Develop clear columns around buyer dilemmas, design decisions, misunderstood ownership issues and real owner experiences. Each article has a distinct useful takeaway, verifiable sources, specific examples, original interpretation, accurate images and editing that removes robotic filler. Attribute real experience only when it exists.
tasks.next_action: Research reader questions and draft the next three guides. Obtain owner permissions and qualified review where required. More facts or paraphrasing alone do not make an original article.

tasks.acceptance: First wave: 12 substantial original guides across at least three demand-supported topic clusters, with source checks, useful visuals, internal links, accurate scope, named responsibility and an update plan. Then expand toward 50 only when usefulness and demand justify each page. Verify the current article/indexed-URL baseline instead of assuming 26.

tasks.title: Originality: end Wikipedia-derived editorial dependence while preserving lawful photo credits
tasks.acceptance: Audit article text, summaries, biographies, generated snippets and assistant sources. Replace inherited wording with independent research and original interpretation from primary sources or permissioned firsthand evidence. Remove public Wikipedia links/references except any necessary Terms disclosure. Preserve required creator/licence attribution, including Commons credits until a lawfully licensed replacement exists.
tasks.next_action: Broaden CONTENT-02 from visible wording to editorial provenance. Investigate inherited assets individually; do not disguise paraphrases or remove mandatory credits to make the site look independent.

tasks.title: Visual explanations: add useful sourced charts and diagrams across the site
tasks.acceptance: Start with six visuals on relevant high-value pages: user-input cost breakdown, fuel break-even, version checklist, recall/VIN decision flow, design timeline and sourced dimension/feature comparison. tasks.title: Subscriptions: validate what readers would pay for and why they would return
tasks.acceptance: Interview at least ten target users and test demand for saved research workspaces, source-backed model coverage, version comparisons, useful alerts and expanded grounded chat. Determine primary country/market, buyer versus enthusiast segments, willingness to pay, repeat-use interval, current conversion/return rates, source licensing, answer accuracy/support burden and cost per active user. Produce an evidence-based go/no-go decision.
tasks.next_action: Start with CONTENT-04 buyer testing and AI-04 usage/cost evidence. Test a 30-day buying pass alongside a recurring enthusiast plan; do not infer subscription demand from catalogue size.

tasks.title: Subscriptions: define a valuable free tier and paid buying/ownership workspace
tasks.acceptance: Document an understandable tier matrix and working prototype. Free retains the catalogue, core articles, sources, essential viewing/safety guidance and a bounded chat allowance. Paid adds validated workflow benefits such as account-synced research, advanced comparisons/export, useful updates and higher grounded-chat limits. Price, geography, refunds, ads and limits are explicit. Test pricing and retention; no claim of unlimited AI.
tasks.next_action: Prototype the offer before billing implementation. Treat example chat allowances as hypotheses, select quotas from actual cost/usefulness, and avoid paywalling generic encyclopaedia facts or essential recall instructions.

tasks.title: Subscriptions: implement billing, accounts and server-side access rights
tasks.acceptance: After offer validation and merchant decisions, ship hosted checkout, customer billing portal, monthly/annual or pass products, account linkage and server-side access checks. Verify signed, idempotent webhooks; reconcile payments, renewals, cancellation, refunds, disputes and failed payments. Define tax/invoice handling, supported countries/currencies, terms/privacy and support. Test checkout and cancellation end-to-end before accepting money.
tasks.next_action: Evaluate Stripe Billing/Checkout or a merchant-of-record alternative based on entity, countries and tax/support responsibility. Decide the merchant and pricing first. Do not trust browser plan flags or grant access merely from a successful redirect.

tasks.title: Paid chat: meter free and paid usage without exposing private budgets
tasks.acceptance: Associate usage with verified accounts; define free and paid successful-answer allowances, context/token caps, reset periods and transparent remaining balance. Enforce atomic limits, concurrency/rate abuse protection and total spend caps server-side. Handle retries/provider failures fairly, provide notice before charging/upgrading, log actual provider usage/cost and protect private inputs. Validate unsupported-model refusal and source links at both tiers.
tasks.next_action: Instrument per-answer cost and usefulness first. Model free allowance, paid allowance and optional credits; keep public demos bounded. The current shared 20-call daily cap is not a per-reader billing system.

Define continue/change/stop criteria from tested willingness to pay and costs.
